bull.b: RenovoRx's device-led model yields very high gross margins (Q1 85.1%, TTM ~79%), signaling strong per-procedure economics. Durable unit economics mean incremental procedures can flow to the bottom line faster as fixed costs are leveraged, improving long-term path to profitability once volumes scale.

The installed-base expansion (16 active centers, 48 total pipeline) and physician advocacy create a durable distribution channel. A growing network increases repeat procedure potential and conversion optionality, supporting predictable ramping of procedure volumes over the medium term as trial sites convert to commercial use.

bull.t: Low leverage and reinforced cash runway
bull.b: Very low debt and a successful $10M placement materially reduce near-term refinancing risk. The strengthened equity position and ~$12.4M cash give management time to convert centers, advance commercialization and finish the pivotal trial before needing sizable new capital, improving strategic optionality.

bear.b: RNXT's operating cash flow remains deeply negative (~-$11.3M TTM), reflecting ongoing burn tied to R&D and SG&A. Persistent cash consumption erodes runway absent rapid revenue scale, forces recurrent financing, and limits financial flexibility—creating a durable constraint on execution and growth options.

bear.t: Modest absolute revenue and reliance on conversions
bear.b: Despite strong growth rates, absolute revenue is small (Q1 $563K; TTM ~$1.49M), meaning profitability hinges on converting evaluation centers and smoothing historically 'chunky' order timing. This reliance on execution at site level makes durable revenue scaling uncertain over the next 2–6 months.

An active Nasdaq bid-price deficiency and an extended compliance deadline through Dec 28, 2026 present a structural market-access risk. Potential delisting or ongoing listing uncertainty can impair liquidity, raise cost of capital, and complicate future equity raises or partnerships if unresolved.
